Quick technical readout from SRE:
- Initial log sampling shows an uptick in batch‑queue latency on the decode workers between 08:37–08:54.
- Several workers reported increased page‑faults around the same window; looks correlated with a GC spike in the model process.
- KV cache growth appears to be caused by a small customer workload that introduced long prefixes (repeat warmup tokens) — cache keys expanded ~3x for that router path.
- No config deploys were recorded in the customer account during the window per our control plane logs.

Suggested immediate mitigations (we can run as hotfix):
- Patch a temporary cap on per‑request KV key list length (runtime flag) to reduce cache expansion.
- Force a rolling restart of the three highest‑load workers with a tuned kernel profile (reduce page‑faults).
- Temporarily enable model‑variant fallback for the heaviest route to an earlier quantized version for 60 minutes.

I’ll prepare a short runbook and roll the hotfix if we have customer permission. Planning note: these mitigations are low‑risk but may cause a brief blip (~60–120s) on restart.

Laura Bennett
Senior SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Thank you for the sync earlier. Short executive summary and timelines: 
- What happened: transient KV cache explosion on a single high‑traffic route caused increased page‑faults and GC activity on three worker nodes, which cascaded into throughput loss and elevated 502/503 rates.
- What we did (completed by 12:05 PDT 06/10): applied per‑route KV cap, rolled the three affected workers with tuned kernel profile, and enabled a 60‑minute fallback to the previous quantized model.
- Impact: p95 latency returned to baseline within ~9 minutes after the rolling restart. Sustained 502/503 rates dropped to <0.2%.
- Next steps:
  1) We’ve scheduled a follow‑up remediation to harden the caching logic in the next patch (SERV‑672) — ETA 2026‑06‑18.
  2) Laura will run a postmortem and share a short timeline + RCA doc to the Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/ops/willowhr/incident-20260610.
